decision: Export DictaBERT-large-char-menaked to ONNX at a pinned revision and publish it on the model mirror, so nikud stops falling back to Nakdimon.
options: A: export with scripts/models/export-menaked.py and publish as a GitHub Release `models-dictabert-char-menaked`, read through the model-mirror proxy (decision 15.9)
B: use the third-party dicta-onnx export (not endorsed by Dicta)
C: keep Nakdimon only and drop the ≥95% target
why: The model card is CC BY 4.0 (attribution only), which the licence gate allows; the export script checks the card's licence and every assumption about the custom head, and prints the registry `files` entry. B is an unreviewed third-party artefact; C gives up the plan's quality target. Hosting follows the decision already taken (15.9: GitHub Releases + CORS proxy).
changes: models/registry.json: the "dictabert-char-menaked" entry's `files` (sha256, size, licence, attribution) — pasted from the export script's output
Vercel env VITE_MODEL_MIRROR_URL (deploy-side) once the edge-workers/model-mirror proxy is deployed
cmd: python -I scripts/models/export-menaked.py --revision <commit sha from the model card> --out out/dictabert-char-menaked  (needs torch, transformers, onnx, onnxruntime; huggingface.co is blocked in the cloud)

decision: Choose a Hebrew neural TTS voice whose weights AND training data allow shipping it; #611 is already in verify/train-7.
options: A: train/fine-tune a Piper voice on a commercially licensed Hebrew corpus (or the owner's own recordings) and pin it with `npm run tts:voice`
B: Phonikud TTS checkpoints (non-commercial: rejected by the gate)
C: stay on the system voice (Web Speech / OS) and leave MOS/latency targets open
recommendation: C now, A as the follow-up task
why: The Phonikud checkpoints are marked non-commercial (cc-nc), and scripts/lib/tts-voice.mjs refuses NC/GPL weights or data, so B cannot ship. No permissively licensed Hebrew neural voice was found in this round; A needs a corpus whose licence the owner signs off. C keeps the feature honest: the code (#611, 87624fb27e) is merged and waits for a voice.
changes: `npm run tts:voice -- …` writes the voice pin (see scripts/tts-voice.mjs --help); nothing changes until a voice is chosen

decision: Pin the two diarization networks (pyannote segmentation-3.0 and a speaker-embedding model) and record 5 golden meetings for DER ≤ 20%.
options: A: segmentation = onnx-community/pyannote-segmentation-3.0 (MIT); embedding = a WeSpeaker VoxCeleb ResNet34 ONNX (CC BY 4.0)
B: embedding = 3D-Speaker ERes2Net/CAM++ ONNX (Apache-2.0)
C: leave diarization off (feature stays unreachable)
recommendation: A for segmentation; B for the embedding if its ONNX input matches `feats` (Kaldi fbank), else A's WeSpeaker
why: segmentation-3.0 is MIT; Apache-2.0 (B) has no attribution chain to carry in the UI, CC BY 4.0 needs a credit line (models credits screen exists, #429). The pin script refuses NC/ND licences and checks revision/sha256/bytes. DIARIZATION_MODELS stays null until both are pinned, so nothing downloads by accident.
changes: src/meetings/diarizePins.ts: DIARIZATION_MODELS.segmentation and .embedding (repo, revision, file, bytes, sha256, license) — the pin script prints the exact lines
cmd: node scripts/meetings/diarization-pin.mjs --model segmentation --repo onnx-community/pyannote-segmentation-3.0 --revision <40-hex> --file onnx/model.onnx --bytes <n> --sha256 <64-hex> --license MIT
